comparison: Perfect agreement on the main conclusions (C2, C3, C44, C46). Both evaluations find the two-stage computation model well-supported. OpenEval emphasizes integration of experimental and modeling results, while peer reviewers highlight the extension of functional understanding beyond pre-existing hypotheses. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Divergent evaluations of the same claims (C55-C59) about inhibitory sources. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting these are speculative and require future validation. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, accepting that identifying inhibitory sources is beyond scope and appropriately presented as open questions. Different interpretation of how to evaluate acknowledged speculation.

Strong agreement on computational modeling (C29-C32, C34-C35). Both find the modeling rigorous and well-validated. OpenEval emphasizes that transfer impedance rather than IPSC changes explains somatic IPSP detection. Peer reviewers praise improved model description and realistic parameters. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Strong agreement on inhibition effects on EPSP properties (C36-C41). Both find converging evidence from modeling and experiments. OpenEval notes quantitative measurements with pharmacological controls. Peer reviewers emphasize physiological significance of shunting and timing effects for coincidence detection. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Strong agreement on anatomical findings (C11-C13, C18-C19). OpenEval emphasizes quantitative consistency and appropriate sample sizes. Peer reviewers describe this as 'one of the most complete descriptions of any neuron.' OpenEval also includes C43 not mentioned in peer review. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Strong agreement on Ia SGN dominance (C14-C17, C47). OpenEval emphasizes genetic labeling, cell counting, and alignment with cat studies. Peer reviewers praise the immunohistochemical and genetic methods. OpenEval also includes C48 not in peer review. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Strong agreement on pharmacological detection of IPSPs (C24-C27). OpenEval emphasizes the logical experimental progression and controls. Peer reviewers acknowledge the approach to overcome leak current limitations and find convincing evidence of glycinergic input. OpenEval also includes C28 on receptor subtypes. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Agreement on electrophysiological methods (C20-C21, C23). OpenEval emphasizes control for technical confounds and statistical testing. Peer reviewers accept findings without challenge, noting clarification of functional inhibition. OpenEval also includes C22 and C51 not mentioned in peer review. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Agreement on functional interpretations (C49-C50, C52). OpenEval notes these are reasonable inferences based on Ia SGN dominance and known SGN properties, though remaining functional predictions. Peer reviewers accept these as discussion points supported by citations. OpenEval also includes C48 and C51 not in peer review. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

OpenEval evaluates claims C45, C53-C54 about in vivo studies and subthreshold integration as SUPPORTED based on citations and consistency with experimental findings. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific claims.

OpenEval evaluates background/context claims (C1, C4-C10) about octopus cells and auditory system as SUPPORTED based on appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as reviewers typically do not explicitly evaluate background claims.
